summary: Iter32 - profile-picture upload bug fix (frontend auth-token-routing). The user-reported 'Not found.' on the installed APK was caused by saveAuth() being bypassed at verify-otp + /auth/session, so session_token never landed in SecureStore and the global authenticated-fetch wrapper had nothing to attach. Verified ALL three fixes from this iteration are working: (1) saveAuth() split — after fresh email-OTP login on the web preview, session_token lives ONLY in @secure:film_companion_session_token (len=40, SecureStore-backed), and the @film_companion_auth blob contains user_id/email/name/picture/is_new_user with NO session_token leakage. (2) Global installAuthenticatedFetch() wrapper works end-to-end: GET /api/auth/me with no manual Authorization header returned 200 + correct user payload, proving the wrapper auto-injects 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' for /api/* calls. (3) onboarding.tsx passes userId={userId} prop to <PhotoUploadStep> (confirmed in source). Backend regression (iter31 pytest suite, 19 tests, re-run as iter32 regression): 19/19 PASS — happy-path JPEG/WEBP, all 8 HEIF brands (hvc1/heix/heim/heis/hevc/mif1/msf1/avif), 3 error-path tests (garbage→400, plain-text→400, oversized→400), BOLA cross-user→404, no-auth→401, batch happy-path (3 pics), batch BOLA→404, batch no-auth→401, post-upload GET persistence. The original user-reported require_owner 404 path is gone: when the right session_token is in SecureStore and userId is correctly passed, upload returns 200; when body.user_id differs from session-resolved id, upload correctly returns 404 (BOLA); when no auth is sent, upload correctly returns 401.

critical_code_review_comments: PhotoUploadStep.uploadPicture sends NO explicit Authorization header — it relies entirely on the global installAuthenticatedFetch wrapper. Verified the wrapper is correctly installed at app boot (root _layout.tsx) and works (validated via /api/auth/me 200 without manual header). This is intentional, but worth a comment in the code so future maintainers don't 'fix' it by re-adding manual headers.

The legit-user-id check in PhotoUploadStep.uploadPicture is brittle: `userId.startsWith('user_') && !/^user_\d{13,}$/.test(userId)`. It assumes backend user_ids always start with 'user_' and are NOT 13+ digit timestamps. Real ids look like 'user_57de60b99dfd' (alphanumeric suffix), so the regex correctly rejects only the legacy `user_${Date.now()}` pattern. Works today, but a brittle contract — consider validating via getAuth() instead of regex.
server.py is 3920+ lines (unchanged since iter31). Worth splitting into routers/* for maintainability.

rca_of_issue: Original user bug (APK photo upload showed 'Not found.'): three independent gaps stacked. (1) The auth screen wrote raw verify-otp / /auth/session JSON to AsyncStorage via `AsyncStorage.setItem('@film_companion_auth', JSON.stringify(data))`, including the session_token. The global fetch wrapper, however, reads the token via `_loadSecret(TOKEN_KEY)` which only looks in SecureStore (native) or `@secure:film_companion_session_token` (web fallback) — so the wrapper saw no token and attached no Authorization header. Cookies (session_token cookie set by /api/auth/verify-otp) still partially worked because of `credentials:'include'` on some calls, but only on web — APK cookies for cross-origin XHR aren't reliable in installed RN apps. (2) PhotoUploadStep.initAuth had a `user_${Date.now()}` fake-id fallback when getAuth() returned nothing — guaranteed 404 from require_owner. (3) onboarding.tsx didn't pass userId, forcing PhotoUploadStep into the storage-race path on every mount. FIX VERIFICATION: (a) replaced both AsyncStorage.setItem call-sites with `await saveAuth(data)` in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx lines 100-101 and 255-256 — confirmed via DevTools that session_token is now in @secure:* (40-char value) and absent from @film_companion_auth. (b) removed the fake-id fallback in PhotoUploadStep.tsx initAuth (lines 53-68) — userId stays empty when unauthenticated, and uploadPicture's guard rail (lines 130-141) surfaces 'Session expired' instead of silently 404ing. (c) onboarding.tsx line 418 now passes userId={userId} to <PhotoUploadStep>. End-to-end: fresh login → /api/auth/me returns 200 via the global wrapper → upload would succeed if the user reached that step. Backend regression 19/19 still pass.
